explain.say: Imagine a bus in Lagos pulling away from a traffic light. This curve shows how far it has gone as the seconds tick by. Look at the yellow mark: the curve is almost flat. The bus has barely moved yet.

explain.say: Here is the key idea. Speed is distance divided by time, and on this graph that is the slope, the steepness. A flat line means stopped. A steep line means fast. Is the curve flat or steep at the yellow mark?

explain.say: Now look at the cyan mark. The curve tilts up more. Each second the bus covers more metres than the second before. That means it is speeding up, which we call accelerating.

faq.q: How do you find speed from a distance-time graph?
faq.a: Find the slope: distance gone divided by time taken. On a curve, the slope of the tangent at a point gives the speed at that instant.
asks: How do I get speed from the graph?

faq.q: Why does the curve get steeper?
faq.a: Because the object covers more distance each second than the second before. Its speed is rising, so the slope rises.
asks: Why is a curved distance-time graph speeding up?

faq.q: What does a flat line mean on a distance-time graph?
faq.a: A flat line means the distance is not changing, so the object is standing still. Its speed is zero.
asks: What does horizontal mean on a distance-time graph?

faq.a: Acceleration is how fast the speed changes. On a distance-time graph it shows as the curve bending upwards, getting steeper and steeper.

faq.q: What is the difference between average and instant speed?
faq.a: Average speed is total distance divided by total time, the slope of a straight line from start to end. Instant speed is the slope of the curve at one moment.

facts: On a distance–time graph, the gradient equals the speed.
A car covering 100 m in 10 s has an average speed of 10 m/s, which is 36 km/h.

quiz.say: On a distance–time graph, what does the slope show?
quiz.show: On a distance–time graph, what does the slope show?
quiz.why: Slope is distance change divided by time change, which is speed.

wrong.1: Distance is read off the up axis, not the slope.
wrong.2: Time is read off the across axis.

quiz.say: A distance–time graph is a flat line. The object is…
quiz.show: A distance–time graph is a flat line. The object is…
quiz.why: If distance does not change, the object is not moving.

wrong.0: Fast motion makes a steep line, not a flat one.
wrong.2: Speeding up makes a curve that gets steeper.
